bull.b: Rapid DTC growth strengthens On’s control over pricing, customer relationships, and product presentation while supporting a richer channel mix. A larger owned-channel base can improve brand consistency and margin durability, reducing reliance on third-party retail partners over the coming quarters.

The combination of sustained low-20s growth guidance and high profitability indicates that On is scaling without sacrificing its premium economics. Maintaining a 65% gross margin and near-20% EBITDA margin would provide substantial resources for marketing, innovation, retail expansion, and geographic growth.

Growth beyond core running footwear broadens On’s addressable market and creates more opportunities to increase customer purchase frequency. Strong apparel and training performance, alongside planned football and golf expansion, can diversify revenue while extending the brand across additional sports and lifestyle occasions.

bear.b: Slower wholesale growth and promotional conditions can pressure sell-through, channel productivity, and the timing of revenue recognition. Although management is deliberately protecting full-price integrity, prolonged weakness in multi-brand retail would make the growth trajectory more dependent on continued DTC execution and successful product launches.

A 30% inventory increase creates an execution requirement as management calibrates wholesale sell-in and navigates uneven retail demand. If inventory does not convert into full-price sales, the company could face greater working-capital needs or increased discounting, which would challenge the durability of current margins.

Higher U.S. import tariffs introduce an external cost burden that can reduce gross-margin flexibility or require pricing and sourcing adjustments. The timing of anticipated refunds is also uncertain, so near-term cash generation and profitability may not fully benefit from the expected relief within the next several quarters.
